execution_description: Separate Claude subagent context in a cloud Claude Code session (round-2 cross-review after reading the four other round-1 reviews); same model family as the designer; not an independent human or vendor.

findings.claim: I confirm the captive-hinge blocker (MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN, V4) and add three things measured on the exported STEP files. (1) A separate pin, the fix that MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN and my own R1 proposed, is necessary but not sufficient. Even with the printed pin removed, the shell-integral stop post sits directly inboard (-y) of the stop tongue and blocks the only workable insertion path, a +y slide from inside the shell. (2) The 'open-ended pin, barrel slides on axially' route (V4 option and my R1 option a) is invalid for this layout. The skin piece sits in the window with about 0.3 mm of z clearance, so the button cannot travel axially along any pin by its 7 mm barrel length. (3) Insertion from outside through the window is impossible because the barrel (x -14.6..-9.4) lies outside the window opening (x -10.4..14.4). Under the current shell geometry no fix limited to the pin produces an assemblable product.
evidence: Probe (CadQuery 2.8, BRepExtrema distance + boolean overlap on shell/button model.step; printed pin between tabs subtracted to simulate a separate pin): pure +y translation of the button at dz=0 is blocked for dy in [-6,-1.2] mm; overlap 8.71 mm3 at dy=-3, 3.91 at -2, 1.03 at -1.4, 0 at -1.1. Every overlap lies in x 10.5..13.5, y <=23.81, z 7.8..9.4, which is the tongue against stop_post.

Same probe with the stop_post box also subtracted: +y path from dy=-11 to 0 is clear at every sample (min distance 0.30 mm, limited by the skin top edge z=18 vs tab_high underside z=18.3; 0.272 at rest).

Search around the post with the pin removed: at dy=-1.19 and dy=-1.6 no offset with dx in {-3.5,-3,-2,0,2,3,3.5} and dz in {-2,-1.7,0,1.7,2} is collision-free, so a translation that sidesteps the post was not found (coarse grid, not a proof of none).

Axial route: round-1 probe moving the button +z 1 mm gives 19.93 mm3 overlap and -z 1 mm 26.93 mm3, and +z 0.3 mm already reaches contact (skin top on tab_high). A 7 mm slide along the pin axis is impossible regardless of which tab is removed.
Recipe: barrel_outer r 2.6 at hinge x=-12 gives x -14.6..-9.4, and window_gap x -10.4..14.4, so the barrel cannot pass through the window from outside.
Probe: a vertical lift from below the open bottom at dy=-11 (pin and post removed) is clear from dz=-20 to 0 (min 2.6 mm). At dy=-8 the skin piece hits the stop shelf (distance 0 at dz -3..-1).
Probe: a 2 mm diameter corridor along the pin axis below tab_low (z -1..5.6) has 0.0 mm3 overlap with the shell, so a separate pin can be inserted from the open bottom.
MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN required_test and manufacturing remaining_uncertainties already flag that the tongue must clear the stop shelf/post. This probe shows it does not.
findings.proposed_change: Assembly order I would accept for this layout: (1) Print the shell without the integral pin and without the stop post and shelf. Make a Ø2 through-hole in tab_low and a blind hole in tab_high on the hinge axis (-12,25), with a lead-in chamfer at the barrel bore ends. (2) Bring the button in through the open bottom about 11 mm inboard (dy≈-11), lift it to its z band, and slide it +y about 11 mm until a designed outward rest stop seats (see R2-ASM2). The barrel enters between the tabs. (3) Insert a separate pin (steel dowel or M2 screw) from below through tab_low, the barrel and tab_high, and retain it with a press fit in tab_high or a screw head under tab_low. (4) Install from below a switch/stop carrier (PCB bracket) that locates on the pin's lower end or the tab_low hole and carries both the switch and the overtravel stop face. That stop face then approaches the tongue in +z, not along the insertion path. (5) Install the PCB/base. Alternative: keep the stop on the shell but make it a separate snap-in or screw-in post fitted after step 3. Any shell-integral stop that faces +y (resists inward motion) is incompatible with step 2.
findings.required_test: Add sequential path checks that mirror the declared order: (a) button-only translation path (lift at the stated dy, then +y to rest) against the shell with the pin and carrier absent, as a swept/continuous check with min_mm >= a stated assembly clearance; (b) pin translation along +z through tab_low, barrel and tab_high with zero overlap except the declared press-fit zone; (c) carrier translation along +z to its seat with zero overlap against the installed button and shell; (d) re-run all rest, press, stop and housing checks on the final assembly. As a negative control, (a) must FAIL on the current shell (stop post present).

findings.claim: I confirm M1, V1 and my R1 ASM2: no outward rest stop. First outward contact is at +3.7 deg in my probe, +3.5..4 in M1 and +3.9 in V1, all at the hinge-side window edge x≈-10.4, with the far face about 1.7 mm proud. Three independent probes agree. The proposed fixes, however, constrain assembly. Any outward stop that is fixed to the shell and engaged by a button feature moving +y (an inner lip on the skin piece larger than the window, as in V1(a), or a button stop face on a shell lug as in M1(a)) is compatible with the +y-from-inside insertion in R2-ASM1, because the lip arrives at its seat last. But it permanently rules out insertion from outside (already impossible), and the lip must avoid the tabs. A lip on the hinge-side end (x≈-10) would collide with tab_low/tab_high (x -15..-9). It would also have a very short lever (about 2 mm), so 0.3 mm hinge play would let the far face move many times that. M1(a)'s 'small spring or flexure' preload, and M1(b)/V1(b) zero free play with stem preload, make the preload depend on carrier position. The preload can only be set at step 4, so it must reference the pin datum (see R2-ASM3). I keep this as major rather than blocking from the assembly side: R2-ASM1 already forces 'revise', and gravity does not drive rotation about the vertical hinge axis in normal use. I do not contest the mechanism and verification roles' blocking rating for F2/F4.
evidence: Round-1 probe: outward rotation about (-12,25,z): +2 deg 0.183 mm, +3 deg 0.075 mm, first contact by bisection at +3.698 deg at button point (-10.4,31.25,10.0); the far-edge lever is about 26.7 mm, so about 1.7 mm protrusion.
mechanism.json M1 evidence: +4 deg overlap 0.008 mm3 at x=-10.43..-10.40; verification.json V1: +3.9 deg wedge at x≈-10.4, z=10.
Recipe tab boxes x -15..-9 (hinge side). The window_gap edge is at x=-10.4, so the tabs already intrude 1.4 mm into the window x band at the hinge end.

R2-ASM1 probe: the +y slide is clear when the post is removed, so a far-end lip seating on the inner wall at the end of the slide adds no new obstacle along the path, provided it stays at x>-9 and outside the tab z bands.
findings.proposed_change: Put the outward rest stop at the far end of the button (x≈12..16, beyond the window edge at 14.4, or above/below the window in the far half), as an inner lip that seats on the inside of the shell at the end of the +y insertion. Keep it inside the outer skin and clear of the tabs. Define preload either with zero stem free play set by the pin-referenced carrier, or with a separate spring installed before the pin. State which element defines rest.
findings.required_test: Positive-rotation check from 0 to +1 deg with end_max_distance about 0.02 mm, requiring contact on the new lip face and not on the window edge. Include the lip in the R2-ASM1 path check (a), showing it reaches its seat only at dy=0. Report face protrusion at the lip-contact pose with the hinge offset by full radial play in +y.

findings.claim: I confirm M2 and V2 on radial hinge play and keep my R1 stack-up finding. V2's counterexample strengthens it. With the button offset +x 0.29 mm inside the designed play, the face hits the window edge at -1.5 deg, before the assumed operating travel is reached, so the switch may never actuate. The assembly route in R2-ASM1 lets the switch and the overtravel stop share one datum, a carrier located on the pin. That is the fix for the floating switch I raised in R1. M2's 'metal dowel in a reamed bore' and MFG-PIN-ANISOTROPY's 'separate metal pin' agree with that route. M2's 0.1–0.15 mm radial clearance also needs coaxial tab holes and barrel bore during pin insertion. The button must be held at rest (lip plus fixture) when the pin goes in, which is another reason to define the rest stop first.
evidence: verification.json V2: +x 0.29 mm offset then -1.5 deg gives 0.0564 mm3 overlap at (14.4,30.21,10.0); stem travel then about 0.36 mm < 0.5 mm assumed operating travel.
Round-1 probe: 0.3 mm translation in any axis brings the button-shell distance to 0; 0.3 mm in -y puts the plunger on the stem.
measurements.json overlap-shell-switch_housing 1.6 mm: switch not located by the shell.
mechanism.json M2 and manufacturing.json MFG-PIN-ANISOTROPY both propose a separate metal pin.
findings.proposed_change: Same as R1 ASM3, plus: locate the switch/stop carrier on the pin end or the tab_low hole (one datum for hinge, switch and stop), set radial play from a printed hole coupon, and write the worst-case stack (play + carrier location + FDM error) against free play, operating travel and stop travel.
findings.required_test: Perturbed-pose checks (button at the corners of the radial and axial play envelope; carrier at its location tolerance): no shell contact before the operating point, operating point reached before stop contact, no stem preload beyond the declared value at rest.

findings.claim: M3 says that moving the button up 0.4 mm drives the skin into the window edge. In this geometry the first upward contact is earlier, at +0.3 mm, where the skin top edge (z 18) meets the underside of tab_high (z 18.3) over x -10..-9. That is where the tab intrudes into the window band (MFG-SUBLAYER-STEP, V2). V2 attributes it correctly. This also limits the R2-ASM1 insertion slide to 0.30 mm clearance. There is a cross-proposal conflict. MFG-ORIENT-SUPPORT wants the barrel top raised flush to z 18 for printing, which gives a 0.3 mm barrel-to-tab_high gap. That equals the skin-to-tab gap and the 0.3 mm tongue-to-shelf gap, so the axial locator is still ambiguous, against M3's request that the barrel ends be the thrust faces with 0.1–0.2 mm.
evidence: Round-1 probe: +z 0.3 mm gives distance 0.0 with no overlap; +z 1 mm gives 19.93 mm3 overlap.
R2-ASM1 probe: on the +y path the constant 0.30 mm minimum distance comes from skin top z 18 vs tab_high z 18.3.
Recipe: tab_high_box z 18.3..21.3 at x -15..-9; window_gap z 9.6..18.4, x -10.4..14.4; barrel z 10.5..17.5; tongue_z_min 7.8 vs stop_shelf_z_max 7.5.
findings.proposed_change: Trim the tabs out of the window band (as MFG-SUBLAYER-STEP and V7 propose). Then choose the axial gaps together: barrel-to-tab smallest (e.g. 0.15 mm), skin-to-window and tongue-to-shelf/carrier larger. If the barrel top is raised for printing, lower tab_high's underside only where it faces the barrel.
findings.required_test: Static clearance at both axial play limits: barrel end faces contact the tabs first; skin, tongue and lip stay clear of the window edge, shelf and carrier.

findings.claim: I confirm M7 and V6, and my R1 ASM4. The stop check passes only on its end pose (continuous bound -0.078 mm, not_proven). V6's finer resampling and my probe both place the nominal contact at the tongue edge on the stop_post face at y≈23.81. If the stop moves to a carrier as I propose, this check must be re-defined against the carrier part, not the shell.
evidence: measurements.json overtravel-stop-engages: continuous_distance_lower_bound_mm -0.0781, continuous_swept_motion not_proven.
Round-1 probe: -2.665 deg contact at (13.47,23.81,7.8..9.4); -2.8 deg overlap 0.059 mm3.
findings.proposed_change: Split into a clearance sweep to just before the stop and an end-pose engagement that names the stop face's part (shell or carrier).
findings.required_test: Sweep 0..0.99*stop with a positive certified bound, plus an end-pose contact located on the declared stop face.

evidence_inspections.observation: Viewed in this reviewer context; sha256 re-checked unchanged. Exterior iso: orange button face flush in the side window of the blue shell, with a thin gap line. No hinge, pin, stop, switch or assembly direction is visible from outside.

Parsed; sha256 re-checked unchanged. recipe_build record for subject bc37a85d. shell_part = union(shell_open, tab_low, tab_high, pin, stop_shelf, stop_post), with stop_post y 21..23.81 and z 6..9.4 directly inboard of the tongue. No insertion-path, assembly-order or positive-rotation check.

Viewed in this reviewer context; sha256 re-checked unchanged. Shows the closed barrel eye at the hinge end, the arm, rib, plunger block and a downward tongue at the far end. The tongue hangs below the skin's lower edge, which is the feature trapped by the shell stop post during +y insertion.

Parsed; sha256 re-checked unchanged. overall_verdict unknown. Rest clearances are 0.272 mm (shell), 0.200 mm (stem) and 1.300 mm (housing). Shell to housing is 1.6 mm. The overtravel stop sweep is not_proven (lower bound -0.078 mm) and passes on its end pose. Rotation checks are negative-only. The scope excludes hinge play.

Viewed in this reviewer context; sha256 re-checked unchanged. The window opening shows the vertical pin between the lower and upper tabs at the hinge end, joined to the wall. The open bottom of the shell (not visible in this view) is the only access for button and pin insertion.
Viewed in this reviewer context; sha256 re-checked unchanged. A plain rectangular placeholder block with no mounting or locating features, so a carrier/PCB datum must be added for it.

Viewed in this reviewer context; sha256 re-checked unchanged. A plain rectangular stem placeholder with no spring or travel modelled. Preload or free play therefore depends entirely on where the (unlocated) housing is placed.

remaining_uncertainties: My insertion-path probes are sampled translations (about 0.1–3 mm steps) on re-imported STEP with the pin and post removed by simple boolean cuts. They are not continuous certificates, and the grid search around the post does not prove that no combined rotation+translation path exists.
The carrier/PCB bracket I propose does not exist in the CAD. Its stiffness, location tolerance and interaction with the real PCB and switch are unknown.
If the hinge is relocated (REQ-pressability and M5 suggest moving the pivot), the whole insertion path changes and must be re-checked from scratch.
Pin retention method (press fit, adhesive or screw), printed hole accuracy and the radial play actually achieved are uncalibrated.
Real mouse shell, PCB and switch were not provided; the open-bottom access and internal volume belong to the stand-in shell only.
Round-2 cross-review is by a same-family model in a separate context; no human or physical assembly trial was performed.
